clue.text: Number of games to support check

parts.note: in tennis a set is a number of games played as one unit
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: Someone counts up the games played before backing a cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback is a check or reverse that halts progress, a synonym in the sense of a hindrance.

clue.text: Periodic table ends up with a lot of ducks in it

indicators.note: in it means the bird goes inside the reversed piece
up in a down clue means reading bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: the end of the word table after its first part, tab, is gone

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all of the bird's name is used

parts.note: the pochard is a diving duck

explanation.surface: The chemists' periodic table is overturned with ducks sitting in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LE into EL; 'a lot of' trims POCHARD to POCHA, which goes 'in it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Epochal means relating to an epoch, a period, so it is a fancy synonym of periodic.

clue.text: Sort of study to follow 16

definitions.meaning: a ... study is a state of deep thought
Gordon ... succeeded Tony Blair as Prime Minister

explanation.definitionFit: A brown study is a reverie, and Gordon Brown was the Prime Minister after Blair.

clue.text: Tory with some US input after 3

indicators.note: input means something is put into the Tory word

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, a Tory
Amer is a shortened form of American, part of the word for the US

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician takes advice from America.
explanation.definitionFit: David Cameron became Prime Minister after Gordon Brown, the subject of clue 3.

clue.text: Live telecommunicators about to put on what they'll never get back

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the next one

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
to add is to put on extra
BT is British Telecom, the UK phone company

explanation.surface: A phone company is about to bill customers for money it will never recover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' looks like a broadcast adjective beside the phone firm, but it is a verb; British Telecom is the UK phone company.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad debt is a loan that will never be repaid, so the lenders never get the money back.

clue.text: God's ahead when it comes to love

parts.note: a poll is a head, so a head is a poll
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A deity takes the lead in matters of the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Split ahead as a head: poll is an old word for head.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo is the Greek and Roman god of music, poetry and the sun.

clue.text: Dog when kept by Disraeli, say, familiarly?

indicators.note: kept by means the short word is held inside the nickname

parts.note: Benjamin Disraeli, called by a pet name, becomes Benji
as means when

explanation.surface: A Victorian Prime Minister keeps a pet hound.
explanation.walkthrough: Disraeli's first name was Benjamin; familiarly it shortens to BENJI.
explanation.definitionFit: The basenji is an African breed of hunting dog that does not bark.

clue.text: Disraeli etc gives page setter in Italian city troubled rest

indicators.note: in means the setter goes inside the city

parts.note: Rimini is a resort city on Italy's Adriatic coast
the setter refers to themselves as me

indicators.note: troubled means the letters of rest are disturbed

explanation.surface: Disraeli sends a messenger to a crossword compiler holidaying uneasily in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Disraeli and his like held the office of head of the British government.

clue.text: Trade mark mathematically undefined

definitions.meaning: an emblem identifying a company's goods
the logarithm of zero, written log 0, has no value in mathematics

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as LOG O: the log of zero is undefined.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is a company's emblem, the visual equivalent of a trade mark.

clue.text: Roughly concerned with role played in my lawn?

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the lawn's growth

parts.note: moss is what grows in the setter's lawn, a jokey self-reference
re means concerning or about

indicators.note: played means the letters of role are acted out in a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener talks vaguely about an acting part performed on their grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my lawn' is Araucaria's joke: what grows in the setter's lawn is moss, split around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: More or less is an idiom meaning approximately, the same as roughly.

clue.text: What Susan had, a bright one of 9?

definitions.meaning: the flower black-eyed Susan has a black eye
the folk song Green Grow the Rushes

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are oblique: the flower name black-eyed Susan, and the line about nine bright ones in the counting song.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiner is slang for a black eye, and something that shines is a bright one.

clue.text: Having gentle exterior, I don't allow I might follow 4

indicators.note: having a gentle exterior means that word wraps around what follows

parts.note: mild means gentle
to ban is not to allow

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken person refuses permission, then wonders about succeeding someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 refers to the Tory leader in another clue; this Labour leader hoped to succeed him.
explanation.definitionFit: Ed Miliband, Labour leader when this puzzle ran, hoped to follow David Cameron as Prime Minister.

clue.text: (From English map) Calne etc

indicators.note: From means the letters are produced out of these words by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Calne and similar towns are found on an English map.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: Calne, a town in Wiltshire, England, is exactly what you find on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: Calne is the name of a place, so it and others like it are examples of place names.

clue.text: Visit African country — the last first before most of 21

parts.note: to call on someone is to visit

indicators.note: the last first tells us to bring the final letter of that country round to the front

parts.note: Ghana is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A traveller plans a trip to West Africa, putting the final stop first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last first' moves the final A of GHANA to the front, giving AGHAN.
explanation.definitionFit: James Callaghan was Prime Minister directly before Margaret Thatcher, the subject of the theme clue 21.

clue.text: Book to study after most of 21?

parts.note: a study is a private den or lair

explanation.surface: A reader goes to their den after nearly all of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair became Prime Minister after John Major, whose surname is read as 'most of' the theme.

clue.text: Briefly that extra distance that brings evidence of happiness

parts.note: the extra mile in Matthew's gospel is the second mile, and S is short for second
a mile is a distance

explanation.surface: Going that extra distance brings a cheerful result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go the extra mile' comes from the Bible's 'second mile'; S abbreviates second.
explanation.definitionFit: A smile is the facial expression that shows someone is happy.

clue.text: Eastern astronomers not on line

parts.note: the Magi were the wise men from the East who followed a star

explanation.surface: Wise men from the East are not on a line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Maginot Line was France's fortified border with Germany before 1940.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maginot Line was a famous French defensive line, so this word names a line.

clue.text: A solver's pursuing an inclination to dislike

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so these pieces go behind the others

parts.note: taken as written
a tip is a tilt or inclination
thy is the old form of your, the solver's

explanation.surface: Someone working a puzzle follows a leaning towards hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipathy is a deep-seated aversion, a synonym of dislike as a noun.

clue.text: Middle Eastern 9 losing head

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the Prime Minister's name is dropped

parts.note: Disraeli was a Prime Minister, the answer to clue 9

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister loses his top spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Israeli describes someone or something from Israel, a Middle Eastern country.

clue.text: Egg developer of 9 losing head

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the Prime Minister's name is dropped

parts.note: Thatcher was a Prime Minister, the answer to clue 9

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister is ousted from the top.
explanation.walkthrough: Thatcher was famously ousted by her own party, which the surface echoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatcher brings eggs to the point of hatching, so it develops an egg.

clue.text: Slow in working out predecessor of 15

indicators.note: working out means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A slow person exercises before a predecessor arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Wilson was the Prime Minister immediately before James Callaghan.

clue.text: Saint's part of design to be convenient for article from the East

parts.note: only part of the word design is used here, its closing three letters

indicators.note: from the East means reading right to left, so these words go backwards

parts.note: to suit is to be convenient for someone
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A holy man shares a section of a plan that suits an imported item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the East' turns the suiting word and the article round together, so they read right to left after the piece of design.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignatius of Loyola, founder of the Jesuits, and Ignatius of Antioch are saints.

clue.text: Far off meteor

indicators.note: off means the letters of meteor go wrong and rearrange

explanation.surface: A shooting star is a long way away.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote means distant, a synonym of far.

clue.text: See 27
Where it all happens to cure stammering not with cheese

indicators.note: to cure the words is to treat them and set their letters right

parts.note: a stammerer saying not produces n-not

explanation.surface: A remedy for a speech impediment involves avoiding dairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cure' rearranges N-NOT and CHEESE; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: On the scene is an idiom for being present where the action takes place.

clue.text: Scots sweethearts surrounding wrong half of Greenham right after most of 21

indicators.note: surrounding means the pair goes round the scrambled piece

parts.note: jo is the Scots word for a sweetheart, so two of them

indicators.note: wrong means the letters picked are shuffled
half of means only one half of Greenham's letters, here its second half

explanation.surface: Scottish lovers circle the protest camp at Greenham Common in a story of political succession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes the back half of Greenham and 'wrong' scrambles it. Greenham Common was the site of a famous women's peace camp in England; 'most of 21' plays on majority.
explanation.definitionFit: John Major followed Margaret Thatcher as Prime Minister; 'most of 21' plays on majority.

clue.text: Primitive punishment for doing what drugs do?

definitions.meaning: execution by throwing rocks, an ancient penalty
drugs make users stoned, so the jokey sense is making someone stoned

explanation.definitionFit: Stoning is the ancient penalty of pelting someone with rocks, and slang for getting high.

clue.text: Sign on line with volumes

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the sign is followed by the line

parts.note: Libra is a sign of the zodiac
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A star sign is written on a list together with several books.
explanation.definitionFit: A library is a collection of books, so it amounts to volumes.
